name: Measurement of the rate of ν_e+d→p+p+e− interactions produced by 8B solar neutrinos at the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
title: Measurement of the rate of ν_e+d→p+p+e− interactions produced by 8B solar neutrinos at the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory

claim.quote: Comparison of φ^CC(ν_e) to the Super-Kamiokande Collaboration's precision value of φ^ES(ν_x) yields a 3.3 sigma difference, providing evidence that there is a non-electron flavor active neutrino component in the solar flux.

summary.plain: SNO's first result: comparing its own measurement of electron-neutrinos from the Sun to Super-Kamiokande's measurement of all active neutrino flavours showed a difference, hinting that some solar neutrinos really do change type on the way to Earth.
summary.technical: Charged-current 8B solar-neutrino flux measured at SNO, φ^CC(ν_e) = 1.75 ± 0.07 (stat) +0.12/-0.11 (sys) ± 0.05(theor) × 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1; comparison to Super-Kamiokande's elastic-scattering flux yields a 3.3σ difference, evidence for a non-electron-flavour active component in the solar 8B flux; total active flux 5.44±0.99 × 10^6 cm^-2 s^-1, consistent with solar models.

why_it_matters.value: First direct comparison-based evidence from SNO that solar neutrinos change flavour en route from the Sun, ahead of SNO's own solar-model-independent 2002 neutral-current confirmation.
why_it_matters.quote: providing evidence that there is a non-electron flavor active neutrino component in the solar flux
